title: Say it another way
cards: Companies don't take on beginners anymore.
Companies are giving that work to AI now.
They're handing that work over to AI.
What you learn at university might be useless by the time you finish.
It could be out of date by the time you graduate.
What matters is that you can change when things change.
What matters is being able to adapt.
((Before the meeting,)) I spent the weekend going through articles about the new system.
I read up on the new system.
Prepare before you talk to the client((, so you don't look clueless.))
Do your homework before you talk to the client.
((In my first job,)) there was so much new stuff, and I had to get up to speed very fast.
It was a really steep learning curve.
((Nobody taught me.)) I learned it at work, through my own mistakes.
I picked it up on the job, the hard way.
Nobody showed me — I learned it all from books and videos.

speaking: Each of you: two things you **taught yourself** and one you **picked up on the job**. Which took the longest?
Think of a time something was **a steep learning curve** for you. What helped most — a course, **reading up on it**, or someone showing you? Each of you: rank the three and say why.
"**They're handing it over to AI.**" Each of you: two tasks — at work or at home — that AI could do, and one it never should. Agree on the riskiest one to hand over.
Agree on two subjects that could be **out of date** by the time today's ten-year-olds graduate, and one that never will be.
Which card was the hardest? Each of you: two new sentences with it about your own work or life.
